title: mielőtt + Past Tense: What Happened Before

sections.title: The mirror image of *miután*
sections.content: *mielőtt* ("before") also links two past events, but the event named in the *mielőtt*-clause is the LATER one — the main clause describes what happened first. Both verbs stay in the same plain past tense you already know; nothing changes shape just because it's "before" instead of "after".

sections.title: mielőtt + past, past
rows: Before we left, we checked the tickets.
Before I went to bed, I closed the window.
Before he said goodbye, he still hugged everyone.

items.english: Before we left, we checked the tickets. (checking came first)
We checked the tickets before we left. (same order, same meaning)

sections.content: It's easy to read *mielőtt* as if it marked the first event, since it's the first word on the page. It doesn't — it marks whichever event is chronologically LATER. In *Mielőtt elindultunk, ellenőriztük a jegyeket*, the checking (main clause) happened before the leaving (*mielőtt*-clause), even though "leaving" is the first word you read.
